title: Sandpit SDK Contributor Flow & Local Mesh Guide (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc describes a lightweight contributor onboarding flow for SDK engineers using a local "sandpit" mesh that simulates Redwood inference endpoints. Aim is to reduce friction for first-time contributors by providing a reproducible local environment for development, manual QA, and faster PR cycles without needing hosted creds or heavy infra.

Scope / audience:
- Primary: new SDK contributors (interns, external contributors, new hires in first 2 weeks).
- Secondary: SDK maintainers who review PRs and test changes locally.
- Not covered: full Dedicated/Private deployment wiring or perf benchmarking against GPU instances.

Assumptions:
- Contributors have Docker and Node or Python toolchain installed (depending on client language).
- Repo contains a /sandpit folder with docker-compose and a minimal fake-server implementation.
- CI can run headless acceptance tests against the sandpit via docker-compose in CI job.

Key goals:
1) Zero-host-credential first run: contributor can run a quick scenario end-to-end without Redwood API keys.
2) Fast feedback loop: make iterative development (code -> unit tests -> local integration) doable in <10 minutes.
3) Reusable test harness: the sandpit supports both manual exploration and automated test runs.
4) Safety: sandpit returns deterministic responses so flaky tests are minimized.

High-level flow (developer journey):
1) Clone repo + checkout starter branch
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk.git && cd sdk
   - git switch -c feat/my-contrib

2) Start sandpit local mesh
   - cd sandpit
   - docker compose up --build -d
   - Runs: fake-api (HTTP), kv-cache (lightweight in-memory), simple-auth (token acceptance).

3) Point local client to sandpit
   - Bash (Node): export REDWOOD_API_URL=http://localhost:8080 && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sandpit-guest
   - Windows PowerShell: $env:REDWOOD_API_URL='http://localhost:8080' ; $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY='sandpit-guest'

4) Smoke test (example commands)
   - Node: npm run example:chat -- --model=sandpit-chat-small --prompt="hello"
   - Python: python examples/chat_quick.py --url $REDWOOD_API_URL --key $REDWOOD_API_KEY

5) Run unit + integration tests against sandpit
   - npm test -- --runInBand --sandpit
   - pytest tests/ --sandpit --log-level=DEBUG

6) Make change, run targeted tests, iterate, open PR

Sandpit internals (short):
- fake-api: minimal REST server that accepts Redwood API patterns: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings. Configurable response profiles (short, long, streaming).
- deterministic-responses.json: mapping of test prompts to deterministic outputs used for acceptance tests.
- trace-proxy: optional element that records request/response pairs to ./sandpit/records for easier debugging.
- auth-simulator: accepts any token matching sandpit-*, otherwise returns 401.

Developer checklist (pre-PR):
- [ ] run docker compose up and confirm fake-api healthy (curl http://localhost:8080/health)
- [ ] run examples in your language (Node/Python/Go) with sandpit env vars
- [ ] add or update deterministic-responses.json if adding new example prompts
- [ ] run unit tests locally and ensure no sandbox-only failures
- [ ] run linting (npm run lint / tox -e lint)
- [ ] update changelog fragment in /changelog/unreleased/

PR reviewer quick-run guide:
- Start sandpit and run the same smoke example(s) the contributor used. Compare the recorded trace (sandpit/records) against expectation.
- Run acceptance subset: make fast/targeted CI job that runs examples for changed languages only.
- If behavior differs vs main branch, ask for deterministic-responses update or isolate flake.

Telemetry and local assertions:
- Sandpit emits simple telemetry events (span id, handler, latency_ms) to stdout captured by docker logs. We provide a small script sandpit/verify_telemetry.sh that asserts events were emitted for each request in a run.
- Unit tests should assert telemetry keys are present when run with --assert-telemetry flag.

Common contributor tasks and recipes:
A) Add a new client method (e.g., chatWithOptions)
   1. Add exported method in client source and unit tests mocking HTTP layer.
   2. Add integration example under examples/ that calls chatWithOptions against sandpit.
   3. Add deterministic response mapping for the example prompt and update tests.
   4. Run full local build + examples + lint. Open PR with changelog fragment.

B) Fix streaming token handling bug
   1. Reproduce with sandpit streaming profile: sandpit supports --stream-chunker to emulate network chunking.
   2. Use the example that consumes stream and records tokens to sandpit/records.
   3. Write unit test that asserts ordering and completeness of tokens.

CI integration notes (for eng-maintainers):
- Add new job sandpit-integration: pulls docker-compose, brings up sandpit, runs language-specific example scripts, tears down. Keep job time <= 10m by using smaller deterministic responses.
- Cache docker images between runs using registry (recommended).
- Gate sandpit jobs to PRs that touch /client/ or /examples/ paths to reduce CI load.

Troubleshooting (quick):
- docker compose fails on M1/M2: ensure use of --platform linux/amd64 for images that don't support arm. Documented in sandpit/README.md.
- 401 from sandpit: check REDWOOD_API_KEY starts with sandpit- and auth service logs (docker logs sandpit_auth).
- Flaky acceptance: check deterministic-responses.json for prompt whitespace differences; file must be exact match.
- Slow local tests: use --fast-profile environment flag to reduce artificial response delays.

Open questions / future work (non-blocking):
- Add simple UI to visualize recorded traces for maintainers (nice for onboarding demos).
- Expand sandpit to support a lightweight embeddings index for embedder QA flows.
- Provide a single-click devcontainer that preboots sandpit for VSCode remote contributors.

Appendix: tiny commands cheat-sheet
- start: cd sandpit && docker compose up -d --build
- stop: docker compose down --remove-orphans
- run node example: (from repo root) REDWOOD_API_URL=http://localhost:8080 REDWOOD_API_KEY=sandpit-guest npm run example:chat
- view logs: docker compose logs -f fake-api

Notes to self: keep deterministic-responses small, prefer short prompts for CI speed. Consider a separate tiny-sandpit image with only a handful of endpoints for the fastest CI path.

If anything is unclear, ping #eng-devexp or @nora.patel on slack.
